newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ITC opens 3.6 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: India's ITC opens 3.6 pct lower.

text.p: The share of tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd fell 11 rupees, or 3.63 percent, to 292 at the start of Thursday's trading on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) after a government agency arrested company officials for alleged foreign exchange rules violations.
"It's going to get hammered," said broker Ramesh Damani, a BSE member-broker. "ITC will probably stay depressed for some time."

India's Enforcement Directorate arrested a director and three former officials on Wednesday after early morning searches at the offices and homes of top officials, including that of two former chairmen, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

"The search operations were organised and undertaken only after sufficient evidence had been collected indicating FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million," the statement said.
"The material already collected includes documentary evidence and statements of senior executives," it said.
ITC Ltd is 31.7 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc. The rest of its shares are held by Indian financial institutions and the public.
ITC share fell 18.25 rupees, or 5.68 percent, on Wednesday on the news.
On the National Stock Exchange, the stock fell 32.0 rupees, or 9.78 percent, to 295. There was no trade at the bourse on Wednesday.
